channel.description: Recent content in Diary on paper.archive

item.title: Megi Maeuntang at Uiseong Maneul Hwangto Megi, Bucheon
item.description: Spicy catfish stew at Uiseong Maneul Hwangto Megi in Jakdong, Bucheon. Freshwater shrimp make the broth, and a block of ramyeon noodles goes in as a matter of course.

item.title: Yukhoe Sashimi and a DIY Malatang
item.description: Dinner was yuksashimi — sliced raw beef eaten with sesame oil, garlic and green chilli — alongside a malatang cooked at home. Good ingredients, not quite enough broth.

item.title: Samgyeopsal and Beef Sirloin for Lunch, with a Mountain of Minari
item.description: Grilling samgyeopsal and beef sirloin at home, starting at lunch. Half the pan is minari. Onion, potato and a pot of stew on the side, and no drinks today.

item.title: Plant Shopping at Joinfolia in Paju
item.description: We went to Joinfolia in Paju to look around and came home with a few more plants. The place is much bigger than it looks from outside.

item.title: Korean Shabu-Shabu at Home — the Three-Act Dinner
item.description: Tonight's dinner: Deungchon-style shabu-shabu, delivered — with one hack. The beef came from the supermarket, since a tray of shabu-sliced beef costs…

item.title: Yasik — Sea Snail Salad & Blanched Squid, Delivered
item.description: Late-night eating is practically a national sport in Korea — it even has its own word, yasik (야식). Tonight's yasik came by delivery app.

item.title: Baekban — A Proper Korean Set Meal in Paju
item.description: Lunch at Bapsarang, a countryside diner in Paju (north of Seoul), the kind of place Koreans call a baekban-jip (백반집).

item.title: Kkot-Samgyeop (Flower Pork Belly) — Daebit Sikdang, Gaebong-dong
item.description: Korean BBQ night at Daebit Sikdang near home. Their thing is kkot-samgyeop (꽃삼겹, 'flower pork belly') grilled on a dome-shaped stone pan.

item.title: Homesul Night — Kahlúa Milk, Jjukkumi, Yukhoe
item.description: Drinking at home tonight — Koreans call it homesul (홈술, home + sul/alcohol). All the food is takeout. The drink: Kahlúa mixed with milk.

item.title: Dakjang Maekju — My Neighborhood Chicken & Beer Pub
item.description: My local pub, Dakjang Maekju in Gaebong-dong — walking distance from home, which in Korea is a blessing.

item.title: Geoje Panorama Cable Car — Nojasan Observatory
item.description: Riding the Geoje Panorama Cable Car up to the 565m Nojasan observatory, and the view over Korea's southern archipelago from the top.

item.title: Hanchi Mulhoe & Octopus Rice Bowl — Yoonsikdang, Geoje
item.description: Lunch on Geoje Island at a place called Yoonsikdang. We ordered hanchi mulhoe and a rock-octopus rice bowl.

item.title: Dongtae-tang Breakfast on Geoje Island
item.description: Day two on Geoje Island. Breakfast at the pollack-stew place right in front of our lodging.

item.title: Geoje Haegeumgang Cruise — Between Seagulls and Cliffs
item.description: Taking the Haegeumgang sightseeing cruise off Geoje Island, where the seagulls follow the boat close enough to take snacks from your hand.

item.title: Milmyeon on Geoje Island — Woomyeonga
item.description: Found a great noodle place on Geoje Island (south coast of Korea) called Woomyeonga. This one was seriously good.

item.title: Gopchang Jeongol — Korean Intestine Hot Pot in Gaebong-dong
item.description: Tonight's anju (안주 — food you eat while drinking) is gopchang jeongol, at my regular place Yeokjeon Sundae-guk in Gaebong-dong, Seoul.

item.title: Blog Redesign
item.description: Finally gave this old dev blog a facelift. Tech posts will still be the main thing, but from now on I'll also drop everyday records here — mostly…
